I will do it much like last year, only I will keep maize a bit bigger because it feeds the house and usually gives steadier money here than the other crops. I do not start from empty talk, I start from what worked on my land and what I saw in nearby fields. On 11.6 mu with just 2 people at home, I cannot spread myself too thin, so I will keep the work simple and put most of the land into spring maize, then keep some cotton, peanut, and mungbean to spread the risk. Fertilizer costs real money, but losing yield costs more, so I will not cut too hard. For maize I will feed it the heaviest, because if maize is hungry, the ears come small. Cotton I will also feed, and I will watch insects closely because cotton can get eaten fast. Peanut needs phosphate and potash better than too much nitrogen, and mungbean I will keep lighter because it does not need as much. I have well water, so when the sky stays dry I will give water at the key times instead of gambling on rain. I will mostly do what I know: plough where I want a cleaner seedbed, rotary where I want to save labor, and I will stay close to the rates that have held yield for me before.
